nodes.description: Registry public state variable holding the address of the external attribute registry contract.
Constant bytes32 attribute key 'isDepositAddress' used to mark addresses as deposit addresses.
Constructor taking _registry and casting/storing it into the registry state variable.
Public function that derives a shifted address from msg.sender, checks the registry attribute and writes the attribute via an external call.
Payable fallback function that calls registerDepositAddress() and then forwards msg.value to msg.sender.
Caller-controlled address used both as the source of the shifted deposit address and as the transfer recipient.
Unsafe bit operation address(uint(msg.sender) >> 20) which truncates the address to its high 140 bits, enabling collisions/crafted addresses.
External call registry.setAttributeValue(shiftedAddress, IS_DEPOSIT_ADDRESS, uint(msg.sender)) which mutates external state and may call back into this contract.
External value transfer msg.sender.transfer(msg.value) performed in the fallback after the registry external call.
Constructor parameter holding the registry contract address supplied by the deployer.
Local variable in registerDepositAddress storing the truncated high bits of msg.sender.

edges.reason: Untrusted msg.sender is cast to uint and right-shifted by 20 bits, a truncating arithmetic operation on caller-controlled input.
registerDepositAddress reads msg.sender as the source of the deposit address derivation.
The fallback sends msg.value back to the caller-controlled msg.sender via transfer (2300 gas stipend limits reentrancy).
The truncated address computed by the shift is assigned to the local variable shiftedAddress.

The attacker-influenceable shiftedAddress (only high 140 bits of msg.sender) is registered/authorised via the external setAttributeValue call, allowing registration for addresses the caller does not control.
registerDepositAddress invokes the external registry.setAttributeValue call to persist the attribute.
The external registry contract is invoked before state is finalised; a malicious registry can call back into registerDepositAddress and re-enter the registration logic.
The payable fallback calls registerDepositAddress() before transferring the received value.
registerDepositAddress reads the registry state variable to perform hasAttribute and setAttributeValue calls.
The constant IS_DEPOSIT_ADDRESS is used as the attribute key inside registerDepositAddress.
IS_DEPOSIT_ADDRESS is passed as the 'what' argument of the external setAttributeValue call.
The constructor parameter _registry is used to initialise the registry state variable.
The constructor writes the cast _registry address into the registry state variable.

normalization_plan.reason: The _registry parameter is only used once, to initialise the registry state variable inside the constructor, so it can be folded into the constructor node.

The local variable shiftedAddress is a temporary derived solely from msg.sender and is immediately consumed by the external registry.setAttributeValue call, so it can be merged into that unsafe operation node.
